summary: Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche studied under Sera Khandro and Dorje Dradul. He later taught Keith Dowman, Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche, and Sera Khandro.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, Kabilsingh studied at Visva-Bharati University, McMaster University, and Magadh University. She served as Professor of Philosophy at Thammasat University (~1973–2000) and founded the Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women in 1987.
Active in sinology and history and archaeology, Liu earned a PhD at Arizona State University (~2006–2011) under doctoral supervisor Claudia Brown and committee member Jiang Wu.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Lin studied at Temple University (~1985–1991). He was Distinguished Professor at National Chengchi University (~1991–2016) and held visiting and European Chair posts at IIAS and Leiden University (~2007–2008).
Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Cheng Yen became a disciple of Yin Shun in 1963 and founded Tzu Chi.
A scholar of Japanology, Crowley studied under teachers Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip B. Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe, as well as committee member Paul Anderer (~1994–1999).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and sinology, Ho studied under traditional teacher Hsuan Hua and earned a PhD at UCLA (~2004–2010) under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Ho also served as a UCLA Teaching Assistant (~2005–2010).
Active in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology, Huang completed a PhD at the University of Arizona (~1980–1986) under supervisor Jing-shen Tao and teacher Robert M. Gimello.

A Buddhist studies and sinology scholar, Chan studied at CUHK and completed a PhD at UCLA (~1986–1993) under Robert E. Buswell Jr., Benjamin A. Elman, and William M. Bodiford. Chan also worked as a CUHK Teaching Assistant.
Specializing in history and archaeology, Ikeya earned a PhD at Cornell University (~2000–2006), studying under teacher David K. Wyatt and committee member Anne M. Blackburn.
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Hsu studied under traditional teacher Zhenhua and was supervised during doctoral studies by Leslie S. Kawamura (~2006–2011) and James B. Apple (2011–2013).
Active in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Ho held posts at Academia Sinica and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University, where he taught Xiuzhi Zeng.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, Tseng completed a PhD at McMaster University (~2008–2014) supervised by James A. Benn. In ~2016, Tseng became Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Fo Guang University.

A religious studies scholar, Akamatsu studied at Kyoto University (~1907–1910) and the University of Tokyo. He served as the first professor at Keijo Imperial University (1927–1941) and held a post at Yamaguchi University.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Watanabe completed a master's degree at the University of British Columbia (~1991–1994) and a PhD at the University of Calgary (~1995–2000) under doctoral supervisor Leslie S. Kawamura.
Active in Buddhist studies, Corona studied under traditional teachers Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.

A Buddhist studies and sinology scholar, Shyu completed an MA at the University of Hawaii (~-1996) under Jan Nattier and a PhD at Cornell University (~1999–2008) supervised by Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Takenaka studied at Kyoto University (~1969–1971). He served as an associate professor at Hanazono University (~1977–1996) and became a professor at Tokoha University in ~1996.

Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Yoshimizu studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Vienna (1990–1994). She worked at the Naritasan Institute (~1989–1992) and became a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2004).
Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Chogye Shabdrung studied at Sakya College in 2003 under teacher Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.
